title: Violation Points and the Card Conduct Reserve on Cartwise Shopper Payouts
content:
For an instant cashout onto the Everyday Pay Card under Cartwise Shopper Payouts, a card conduct reserve stays on the account: a shopper carrying 6 or more active violation points leaves 40.00, one carrying 1 to 5 leaves 15.00, and one carrying none leaves nothing.

## Training questions answered

**Where do the violation points come from?**
From the shopper's Cartwise Shopper Contractor Accounts record, which carries the shopper's active violation points. Only the active points on that record at the time of the cashout are read.

**What stays on the account at each point count?**

| Active violation points | Card conduct reserve |
|---|---|
| 6 or more | 40.00 |
| 1 to 5 | 15.00 |
| 0 | nothing |

**Where does 5 points fall, and where does 6?**
Five active points is the top of the 1 to 5 band, so 15.00 stays. Six active points reaches the 6 or more band, so 40.00 stays.

**Does a shopper with a very high count keep back more than 40.00?**
No. Every count of 6 or more leaves the same 40.00.

**Does a shopper with no active points keep anything back for conduct?**
No. With zero active violation points no card conduct reserve stays on the account.

**Is the reserve charged to the shopper?**
No. It is a sum that stays on the payout account's balance when the card cashout is worked out; nothing is booked for it.

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A shopper carrying 1 active point: 15.00 stays.
- A shopper carrying 9 active points: 40.00 stays.
- A shopper carrying 0 active points: no card conduct reserve.
